name: Dragon Island
hero_subtitle: A rocky islet in the lagoon whose silhouette looks like a sleeping dragon.

overview.title: A silhouette on the water
overview.p1: Dragon Island (Île du Dragon) is a small rocky island in the lagoon. From the right angle its profile suggests a dragon at rest — a local landmark and photo stop.
overview.p2: You can view it from the shore or, when operators run trips, approach by boat. It is a short highlight, best paired with White Dune or a lagoon drive.
overview.p3: Respect nesting birds and any access rules posted locally.

q1.question: Can I land on Dragon Island?
q1.answer: Access rules vary. Many visits are viewpoint-only or boat approaches — check locally before planning a landing.

q2.question: Where is the best viewpoint?
q2.answer: Ask your camp or driver for the classic silhouette angle across the lagoon.

q3.question: How long does a Dragon Island visit take?
q3.answer: One to two hours including transfer is typical for a viewpoint stop.

q4.question: Is there birdlife?
q4.answer: Possible. Keep distance and avoid disturbing nesting areas.

q5.question: Do I need a boat tour?
q5.answer: Not for distant shore views. A boat is useful if you want to approach the islet more closely.
